hook.line: The ancient Egyptian game of “passing”, played by pharaohs and farmers alike — and likened to the soul’s journey through the underworld.
hook.say: Let me show you the pharaohs’ game!

ch.t: From the banks of the Nile
ch.say: Even kings took it to their tombs.
p: Senet was played in Egypt for nearly 3,000 years. Its name means “passing”.
Fragments of boards come from First Dynasty tombs, and the earliest certain picture is in the tomb of Hesy at Saqqara. Tutankhamun was buried with several boards.

ch.say: Aim for 26, the House of Beauty!
ch.cap: Thirty squares in 3 × 10. The arrows follow the reverse-S track; the last five squares bear signs
p: Go from 1 to 30 in a reverse S and bear off to win. 15 holds the ankh (rebirth), 26 the three nefer signs of the House of Beauty, 27 the House of Water.
28–30 show III, II and the eye of Horus. You move by the white sides of four throw sticks.
